environment.description: Same Spring Boot 3.1 application deployed on ECS Fargate with hardened task definition. Container root filesystem uses readonlyRootFilesystem:true in the ECS task definition containerDefinitions. No tmpfs volumes, no EBS mounts, no EFS mounts attached to the task. The only writable layer available is the container's stdout/stderr stream which routes to awslogs driver with log-driver-options restricting max-buffer-size. Logback is configured with ConsoleAppender only (STDOUT). The application.yml sets app.audit.log.path to /var/log/app/audit.log but since the filesystem is read-only, FileWriter operations in writeAuditEntry() and writeAdjustmentAudit() throw IOException silently caught in the catch block. SLF4J logger.info() calls still execute but output goes only to stdout via ConsoleAppender which is captured by the awslogs driver with awslogs-multiline-pattern set to '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T' ensuring injected newlines in log messages cannot create fake log entries that appear as separate structured events in CloudWatch.
